text:
Cutter Gauthier has turned Anaheim's season into his own highlight package. He has 15 points in his last ten games, he scored again in Wednesday's 7-0 rout of San Jose, and NHL.com's headline on him read "Gauthier Continues to Make History." That win snapped a four-game losing run and came with a 23-save shutout from Laurent Brossoit, our projected starter again tonight.

The Ducks may also get help back. Beckett Sennecke, who had 16 points in his last ten before landing on injured reserve, is off ESPN's injury report, and Leo Carlsson has moved to day-to-day. Ryan Poehling remains out with a knee injury, and Mikael Granlund has filled his spot. The Ducks sit third in the Pacific, seven points ahead of the Kings, with a 44% chance at the playoffs by our numbers.

Los Angeles is better than its spot in the standings. The Kings have taken half the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, but their finishing has cost them 7.1 goals and their goaltending 6.2. Adrian Kempe has gone eight games without a goal on 2.7 expected. Artemi Panarin is back from his own absence, and Drew Doughty just played his 1,300th game with the club. They come in rested, with three days off since a 2-1 win in Montreal, where Darcy Kuemper made 29 saves in Dylan Larkin's Canadiens debut.

Our numbers expect 3.33 goals for Anaheim and 3.11 for Los Angeles. Gauthier sits at 42% to score. Jeff Malott faces the Kings for the first time since leaving them. Our sleepers are both Kings: Corey Perry, who has made the most of a fourth-line role with dangerous shots lately (14% to score), and Alex Laferriere, 54% for a point.
headline: Cutter Gauthier gets the Kings in a division game
